newsitem.title: UK: Clean tankers torpid, especially from Mideast.
newsitem.headline: Clean tankers torpid, especially from Mideast.

text.p: Oil product tanker rates still showed no sign of rising from the doldrums of recent weeks, shipping brokers said on Friday.
The Caribbean market was virtually the only sector that managed to hold its own, with 29,000 tonne Boston beam vessels achieving a healthy W240 on upcoast trips.
But the picture elsewhere was gloomy, and brokers E.A. Gibson said, "A light is not yet discernible as to when the recovery will commence."
They describe the clean market in the east as "appalling" with ever falling levels and quoted W160 as the rate for 29,000-30,000-tonne vessels on long haul voyages from the Gulf.
"The continuing dearth of enquiry from the Singapore market exacerbates the build-up of tonnage in the Middle East which could take a long time to clear," Gibson added in their weekly tanker report.
The Mediterranean market was no livelier, although 27,500 tonne naphtha cargoes managed to hold at a modest W182.5 and there was some interest in moving product east.
Inter-U.K./Cont 20,000 tonne stems remained moribund at W200, as they have been for several weeks, brokers said.
